findings.title: Post-replace fsync failure can unlink the newly committed state file
findings.evidence: The broad exception handler wraps both 'os.replace(tmp_path, path)' and the later directory fsync call, then unconditionally runs 'os.unlink(tmp_path)'. After a successful replace, tmp_path now names the destination file, so any later exception from directory fsync will delete the committed state file.
findings.recommendation: Limit the cleanup handler to the temp-file creation/write/replace phase, or track whether 'os.replace' has already succeeded and skip unlinking once ownership has moved to the destination. For example, call '_fsync_directory(directory)' in a separate try/except after replace, without deleting 'tmp_path' on failure.
